Emma: Quick question from the dealroom — Customer requires primary processing in DE (Frankfurt) with deterministic failover to CA (Montréal). Control plane in US is a no-go for them. They also want BYOK (HSM-backed) in either DE or CA. Any immediate blockers with sub-processors / routing policies / pricing?
Diego: Short answer: hosted Redwood API currently has control plane in US. Two paths: 1) Redwood Private (control plane deployed into customer VPC) — meets control-plane requirement; 2) Dedicated with a regional control-plane option, but that's a heavier commitment.
Diego: For datapath we support eu-central-1 + ca-central-1. We can pin inference routing to those regions. One caveat: some infra pieces (metrics ingestion, analytics) may still talk to our SaaS telemetry endpoints unless customer opts out.
Sofia: We can do Private deployment to meet their control-plane restriction. BYOK via customer-managed HSM/KMS is supported in both AWS eu-central-1 and GCP ca-central-1 (we support external key wrapping + HSM). Need to validate cert chain & peering. Also need to confirm if customer needs air-gapped (on-prem) vs VPC-hosted.
Sofia: Subprocessor note: in DE we may use AWS eu-central-1 (AWS employees for infra ops), in CA we may use GCP ca-central-1 (GCP employees). No third-country subprocessors should touch tenant data if we pin routes and use Private.
Rachel: Legal note — we need to produce the subprocessor list (legal names + countries) and confirm whether logs/telemetry include any headers with US-hosted services. Customer's SQA flagged "no control plane in US" so we must ensure support teams don't route secrets or telemetry through US.
Tarun: For pricing: if they want pinning + BYOK + deterministic failover testing, we should propose a time-limited POC add-on: no Dedicated commit for POC, but small reserved capacity + networking setup fee. Long-term: Dedicated or Private has a platform fee + monthly infra. Also account for egress between EU <-> CA during failover & DR tests.
Emma: Customer metrics: ~150 RPS peak, avg 30k tokens/day, retention window ~7 days, will do canary traffic then cutover. They asked for a ballpark delta vs standard hosted pricing for dedicated/private + BYOK. Also asked for list of subprocessors for procurement.
Diego: @Emma can you confirm whether the customer will manage the KMS (BYOK) in their account or expect Redwood to host keys in their cloud region? If customer-managed keys in their account, setup is straightforward. If Redwood hosts HSM on their behalf, we need add'l compliance review.
Emma: Customer will host keys in their account (they said they have HSM cluster in ca-central-1).
Sofia: Good — customer-managed HSM = fewer legal hoops. We'll need a network peering + IAM runbook and a cert for the control-plane endpoints. I can sketch the network checklist:
```
- VPC peering/privatelink
- TLS cert chain (customer CA or public) for control-plane
- Service account with restricted IAM roles
- KMS grant + key policy review
- Egress rules for telemetry (opt-out path)
```
Diego: For routing policy config during POC we can use something like:
```
routing:
  tenant_pin:
    primary: eu-central-1
    failover: ca-central-1
    control_plane: private
    telemetry_opt_out: true
```
Rachel: I'll pull together subprocessor legal names this afternoon and confirm any US-based support access that might touch metadata. Also will flag ISO/SOC2 docs for the customer.
Tarun: For the quote — I'll produce two SKUs: (A) POC short-term (30 days) — infra setup fee + light reserved capacity + egress budget, (B) Production Dedicated/Private — monthly commit + BYOK integration fee + 99.9% SLA option. Need Sofia's estimate for setup hours.
Sofia: Setup estimate: 40-60 engineer hours for Private deploy + network peering + KMS integration. If customer provides runbook + infra access quickly we can be on-board in ~2 weeks for POC.
Emma: Customer also sent a security questionnaire (attached link). They want confirmation that no user data leaves DE/CA except during failover, and that control plane is not routed via US.
Diego: We can run a short shadowtest to show data locality constraints — we'll capture flow logs and handoff the report. Need SRE contact for log access.
OpsBot: Ticket INF-8932 created: "POC — DE primary / CA failover — BYOK onboarding" assigned to Sofia.
Rachel: I'll add a clause in the SOW stating "no control plane in US for tenant X; telemetry opt-out enabled; subprocessor list provided" — will send draft for review.
Emma: Thanks all — I'll share this thread with the customer and ask for a quick sync tomorrow. @Tarun @Diego please add pricing + routing sample to the deck. :raised_hands:
